learning_goal: Trace one red cell from the placenta back to the placenta, name the three shunts and say what each one bypasses and why, explain why the best-oxygenated blood reaches the brain and the heart, describe what the first breath and the clamped cord change about pressure and resistance, list what each fetal vessel becomes in the adult, and use all of it to explain patent ductus arteriosus, duct-dependent lesions and persistent fetal circulation.

terms: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn

structures.name: Placenta
structures.label: Placenta — where gas exchange actually happens

structures.name: Umbilical vein
structures.label: Umbilical vein — the only truly oxygenated vessel
structures.narration: One umbilical vein leaves the placenta carrying blood at about eighty percent saturation — the highest anywhere in the fetus, and lower than any adult arterial value. Note the reversal that catches students out: in the cord the vein carries the oxygenated blood and the two arteries carry the deoxygenated. It enters the abdomen at the umbilicus and runs up in the free edge of the falciform ligament, which is exactly where you will find its adult remnant.

structures.name: Ductus venosus
structures.label: Ductus venosus — shunt one, past the liver
structures.narration: Most of that blood does not enter the hepatic sinusoids. The ductus venosus carries roughly half of it straight from the umbilical vein into the inferior vena cava, so the liver — an organ the fetus does not need for detoxification while the mother's liver is available — does not slow down the delivery of oxygen. The rest perfuses the liver itself and rejoins by the hepatic veins.

structures.name: Portal sinus
structures.label: Portal sinus and left portal vein

structures.name: Liver
structures.label: Liver — the organ the first shunt goes past

structures.name: Hepatic veins
structures.label: Hepatic veins — the half that did perfuse the liver

structures.name: Inferior vena cava
structures.label: Inferior vena cava — the well-oxygenated stream
structures.narration: The shunted blood mixes with venous return from the lower body and reaches the right atrium at about seventy percent saturation. It arrives as a stream rather than a swirl — this is the single most important idea in the whole topic, because the fetus has no way to separate oxygenated from deoxygenated blood except by keeping the two streams apart as they cross the right atrium.

structures.name: Superior vena cava
structures.label: Superior vena cava — the poorly oxygenated stream
structures.narration: Blood returning from the head and upper limbs enters the right atrium from above, is directed downwards across the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, and barely mixes with the inferior caval stream at all. Two streams, two destinations, in the same chamber.

structures.name: Right atrium
structures.label: Right atrium — where the two streams cross without mixing

structures.name: Interatrial septum
structures.label: Interatrial septum — septum primum and septum secundum

structures.name: Crista dividens
structures.label: Crista dividens — the ledge that aims the stream
terms: free lower edge of the septum secundum
structures.narration: The free lower edge of the septum secundum overhangs the mouth of the inferior vena cava as a ledge called the crista dividens. It splits the incoming stream, sending most of it straight through the foramen ovale into the left atrium and letting the remainder turn down into the right ventricle. The fetus does not mix and then divide; it aims.

structures.name: Foramen ovale
structures.label: Foramen ovale — shunt two, past the lungs and the right heart
structures.narration: Because right atrial pressure exceeds left, the thin septum primum is pushed aside and blood crosses right to left through the foramen ovale. The best-oxygenated blood in the body therefore arrives in the left atrium without ever passing through the lungs or the right ventricle.

structures.name: Left atrium
structures.label: Left atrium — fed across the septum, not by the lungs
structures.group: The left heart and the head

structures.name: Left ventricle
structures.label: Left ventricle — a third of the work before birth
structures.group: The left heart and the head

structures.name: Ascending aorta
structures.label: Ascending aorta — the best blood in the body
structures.group: The left heart and the head

structures.name: Aortic arch
structures.label: Aortic arch and the isthmus
structures.group: The left heart and the head

structures.name: Brachiocephalic, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries
structures.label: Head and arm vessels — supplied before the duct joins
structures.group: The left heart and the head
structures.narration: From the left atrium the blood passes to the left ventricle and out into the ascending aorta, whose first branches are the coronaries and then the vessels to the head and upper limbs. So the two organs that can least tolerate hypoxia, the brain and the heart itself, are supplied first and with the best available blood. Understand the streaming and this arrangement is not a coincidence but the point of the whole design.

structures.name: Right ventricle
structures.label: Right ventricle — two thirds of the work before birth
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs

structures.name: Pulmonary trunk
structures.label: Pulmonary trunk
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs

structures.name: Pulmonary arteries
structures.label: Pulmonary arteries — only enough to grow the lungs
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs

structures.name: Lungs
structures.label: Lungs — fluid filled, and their vessels clamped tight
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs

structures.name: Pulmonary veins
structures.label: Pulmonary veins — almost nothing comes back, before birth
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs

structures.name: Ductus arteriosus
structures.label: Ductus arteriosus — shunt three, past the lungs
structures.group: The right heart and the lungs
structures.narration: The right ventricle pumps into the pulmonary trunk, but pulmonary resistance is so high that only a small fraction reaches the lungs — enough to grow them, no more. The rest crosses the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta, entering below the origin of the left subclavian artery, which is why the lower body receives blood that is less saturated than the head. The duct is held open by low oxygen tension and by prostaglandin E2 from the placenta, and both of those facts become treatment later.

structures.name: Descending aorta
structures.label: Descending aorta — below the duct, and less saturated

structures.name: Common and internal iliac arteries
structures.label: Common and internal iliac arteries

structures.name: Umbilical arteries
structures.label: Umbilical arteries — back to the placenta
structures.narration: Two umbilical arteries branch from the internal iliac arteries, run either side of the bladder and back out along the cord to the placenta, carrying blood at roughly fifty-five to sixty percent saturation for reoxygenation. A cord with only one artery instead of two is worth reporting at delivery, because it carries a raised rate of renal and other anomalies.

structures.name: Flow
structures.label: Flow — direction and volume, at this moment

structures.name: Median plane
structures.label: Median plane — reference

structures.name: Patent ductus arteriosus
structures.label: Patent ductus arteriosus — the same duct, still open
structures.narration: If the duct stays open after birth the pressure gradient has reversed, so flow now runs from aorta to pulmonary trunk — left to right, through both systole and diastole. That is the continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle, with bounding pulses and a wide pulse pressure. It is common in premature babies and classically associated with congenital rubella. Because prostaglandin holds the duct open, a prostaglandin synthesis inhibitor such as indomethacin or ibuprofen closes it.

structures.name: Flow in a persistent duct
structures.label: Flow with the duct still open — now left to right

structures.name: Duct in persistent fetal circulation
structures.label: Persistent fetal circulation — the duct still shunting right to left
terms: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
structures.narration: The transition can also fail on the lung side. If pulmonary vascular resistance does not fall — after meconium aspiration, birth asphyxia, sepsis or with hypoplastic lungs — the foramen ovale and duct keep shunting right to left and the baby stays hypoxic. Hypoxia and acidosis constrict the pulmonary vessels further, so the failure feeds itself. This is why the transition is described as a circulation that must be actively completed rather than a switch that flips at delivery.

structures.name: Flow in persistent fetal circulation
structures.label: Flow when the pulmonary bed never opens

views.title: Two resistances decide everything

ops.kind: an organ the fetus does not yet need is bypassed by
high pulmonary resistance means the right heart is bypassed through
whatever still enters the right ventricle bypasses the lungs through

views.narration:
Start with two numbers rather than a diagram. Pulmonary vascular resistance is very high because the lungs are fluid-filled and their vessels are constricted. Systemic vascular resistance is very low because the placenta is an enormous low-resistance bed. Blood goes where resistance is least, so it avoids the lungs and heads for the placenta, and three shunts exist to let it do that — one past the liver, one past the right heart, one past the lungs. Learn the two resistances and the three shunts stop being a list to memorise.

The fetus breathes through the placenta, not the lungs. The lungs are full of fluid and their vessels are clamped tight, so pulmonary resistance is very high, while the placenta is a huge low-resistance bed that keeps systemic resistance low. Blood therefore wants to go anywhere except the lungs. Three shunts are built to let it: one past the liver, one past the right side of the heart, and one past the lungs. Every fetal peculiarity follows from those two resistances and those three shunts.

views.title: Follow one red cell from the placenta
views.narration: Now walk the whole route once, out loud. Umbilical vein at eighty percent, the highest in the body. Ductus venosus past the liver into the inferior vena cava. Into the right atrium at about seventy percent, aimed by the crista dividens through the foramen ovale into the left atrium. Left ventricle, ascending aorta, coronaries and carotids — the brain and the heart get the best of it. Meanwhile the superior caval stream crosses into the right ventricle, meets a shut pulmonary bed and crosses the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta below the left subclavian. Then out along the two umbilical arteries to the placenta to start again. Say that route until it is automatic; most of the marks in this topic are in it.

views.title: Streaming — why the fetus is not just mixed blood

ops.kind: aiming the inferior caval stream through

views.narration: Cut across the right atrium and look at the two streams. The inferior caval stream is well oxygenated and the superior caval stream is not, and they cross the same chamber without properly mixing. The crista dividens, the free lower edge of the septum secundum, splits the inferior stream and sends most of it through the foramen ovale. That is the mechanism behind the exam favourite: the fetal brain and heart receive the most saturated blood, and the lower body receives the least, because the ductus arteriosus empties into the aorta beyond the head and arm vessels.

views.title: Why the brain gets the best blood

ops.kind: joins below the head and arm vessels, which is why the lower body gets less, at

views.narration: From the left atrium the blood passes to the left ventricle and out into the ascending aorta, whose first branches are the coronaries and then the vessels to the head and upper limbs. So the two organs that can least tolerate hypoxia, the brain and the heart itself, are supplied first and with the best available blood. Understand the streaming and this arrangement is not a coincidence but the point of the whole design.

views.title: Two events at birth, every closure follows

ops.kind: rising pulmonary flow raises the pressure in
losing the placenta raises systemic resistance and lowers the pressure in
left now exceeds right, which presses shut

views.narration:
Two events, and you can derive the rest. The lungs open, so pulmonary resistance falls, pulmonary flow rises and left atrial pressure goes up. The cord is clamped, so systemic resistance rises and right atrial pressure comes down. Left now exceeds right, the flap valve is pressed shut and the foramen ovale closes functionally in minutes. Rising oxygen and the loss of placental prostaglandin constrict the ductus arteriosus over ten to fifteen hours. Umbilical flow stops, so the ductus venosus closes. Then name what each becomes: ligamentum teres, ligamentum venosum, fossa ovalis, ligamentum arteriosum, medial umbilical ligaments — and remember the superior vesical arteries stay open and keep working.

The lungs inflate, the fluid is cleared and alveolar oxygen dilates the pulmonary vessels. Pulmonary vascular resistance collapses, pulmonary blood flow increases many times over, and all that blood returns to the left atrium, whose pressure now rises.

Clamping the cord removes the largest low-resistance bed in the circulation, so systemic resistance jumps. At the same time the umbilical venous return stops, so right atrial pressure falls. Two changes, one result: left atrial pressure now exceeds right for the first time, and it stays that way for life.

The foramen ovale shuts because the pressures reversed and the septum primum is pressed against the septum secundum — no tissue has to grow for that, only for permanent fusion over the following months. The ductus arteriosus constricts within about ten to fifteen hours as oxygen tension rises, placental prostaglandin E2 disappears and bradykinin acts on its muscular wall, and it is anatomically sealed within two to three weeks. The ductus venosus closes once umbilical flow stops. Distinguish functional closure, which happens in hours, from anatomical closure, which takes weeks — that distinction is the whole reason a duct can be reopened with a drug.

views.title: Fifteen minutes old — the duct turns round
views.narration: Watch the arrows in the duct, and nothing else. A quarter of an hour ago they pointed from the pulmonary trunk into the aorta, because the lungs were the hard way round. Now they point from the aorta into the pulmonary trunk. Nothing was rebuilt and no valve moved: the two resistances swapped places, and the blood went the way that was easier, which is the only thing blood has ever done. A normal newborn shunts a little left to right across a duct that is still closing, for the ten to fifteen hours it takes to shut. Hold on to this frame, because a duct that fails to shut is stuck here — and the murmur, the bounding pulses and the drug that treats it all follow from an arrow pointing this way instead of that way.

views.title: What each one becomes
views.narration: Five pairs to know cold. Umbilical vein becomes the ligamentum teres hepatis in the free edge of the falciform ligament. Ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum. Foramen ovale becomes the fossa ovalis, with the edge of the septum secundum as its limbus. Ductus arteriosus becomes the ligamentum arteriosum, and the left recurrent laryngeal nerve stays hooked under it for life. The distal umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments while their proximal parts stay open as the superior vesical arteries — the only fetal vessel on this list that keeps a job.

views.title: When the transition fails — in both directions

ops.kind: the same vessel, after the pressures have reversed, shunting the other way as
if pulmonary resistance never falls, the fetal pattern persists as

views.narration:
The duct can be wrong in either direction. Left open when it should have shut, the reversed gradient makes it shunt left to right — a continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses, and a prostaglandin inhibitor to close it. But in a duct-dependent lesion it is the only connection the baby has, and closing it causes collapse on day two or three; there prostaglandin E1 keeps it open until surgery. The third failure is on the lung side: if pulmonary resistance never falls, the shunts keep running right to left and the newborn stays blue, with hypoxia and acidosis making the constriction worse. Finish every question the same way — trace the blood, name the shunt and the gradient, apply the two birth events, then name the remnant.

If the duct stays open after birth the pressure gradient has reversed, so flow now runs from aorta to pulmonary trunk — left to right, through both systole and diastole. That is the continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle, with bounding pulses and a wide pulse pressure. It is common in premature babies and classically associated with congenital rubella. Because prostaglandin holds the duct open, a prostaglandin synthesis inhibitor such as indomethacin or ibuprofen closes it.

Reverse the logic and you have the most useful fact in neonatal cardiology. In some malformations the only route between the two circulations is the duct itself — transposition, pulmonary atresia, critical coarctation, hypoplastic left heart. Those babies are stable while the duct is open and collapse in the first days of life as it closes. Prostaglandin E1 keeps it open and buys time for surgery. A newborn who is well at birth and becomes blue or shocked on day two or three, especially with absent femoral pulses, is a duct closing on a lesion that needed it.

The transition can also fail on the lung side. If pulmonary vascular resistance does not fall — after meconium aspiration, birth asphyxia, sepsis or with hypoplastic lungs — the foramen ovale and duct keep shunting right to left and the baby stays hypoxic. Hypoxia and acidosis constrict the pulmonary vessels further, so the failure feeds itself. This is why the transition is described as a circulation that must be actively completed rather than a switch that flips at delivery.

provenance.reauthor_note: Re-authored from the sequence engine onto the procedural provider. The structures were teaching BEATS with no geometry; they are now the anatomical parts models3d/fetal-circulation.js builds, and every beat's narration is carried across VERBATIM onto the structure or the view that replaced it. Nothing taught was dropped: one beat that cannot be a view is in deferred_beats with its full text. One view (beat 6) is newly written, for a picture the sequence engine could not show at all — the duct reversing.

gaps: THE ADAPTER PAINTS A STRUCTURE ONE COLOUR, SO THE MODEL'S SOLVED SATURATION DOES NOT REACH A STUDENT. viz3d.js merges every mesh carrying a key into one geometry and gives it one MeshStandardMaterial coloured from the SCENE's color field (or the model's LAYERS palette) - the material the model built, which carries the solved oxygen saturation at that t, is discarded. In a direct render the whole picture recolours as the transition proceeds, and the umbilical vein, inferior cava, ascending aorta, descending aorta and umbilical artery come out in that order by measured pixel warmth (120.8, 87.5, 75.2, 53.3, 52.0 red-minus-blue). In the player they are flat anatomical colours. The scene keeps the original author's colours, which at least carry the vein-artery reversal in the cord, and nothing is shown that is WRONG - but the single best thing this model does is currently invisible in the app. The fix is an engine change and belongs on its own queue item: let the adapter keep the built mesh's own colour when the scene declares none.

THE FLOW LAYER IS ONE STRUCTURE COVERING EVERY VESSEL'S ARROWS, so a view that hides a vessel leaves its arrows hanging in mid air. Measured, not predicted: beats 3 and 4 were first authored isolating a region with the flow layer on, and rendered as a cloud of loose gold cones. The rule applied here is that a view either shows the whole circuit and may show flow, or isolates a region and must not. The better fix is per-vessel marker keys in the model so a view can show exactly the arrows of the vessels it is showing; it is left undone because it would add twenty-odd structures to this scene.

RE-AUTHORED from sequence to model3d on 2026-09-11. The scene previously had teaching BEATS as its structures (the_problem, brain_first, first_breath, cord_clamped, shunts_close, remnants, pda, duct_dependent, persistent_fetal, exam_frame) because it was written for the SVG panel engine. Structures are now the anatomical parts models3d/fetal-circulation.js builds; every beat's narration is preserved verbatim on the structure or the view that replaced it. Nothing taught was dropped.

ONE BEAT WAS MOVED OUT, NOT DELETED - see deferred_beats[]. 'How to answer any fetal circulation question' is exam technique with no frame it could change, and every structure it names is already shown by the view that teaches it.

ONE VIEW IS NEW. Beat 6, 'Fifteen minutes old - the duct turns round', has narration written for this conversion rather than carried over. It exists because the model can show something the sequence engine could not: the arrows in the duct reversing, as a consequence of the solved resistances rather than as an assertion. Every other word in this scene is the original author's.

THE MODEL AGREES WITH THE NARRATION, NOT WITH THE LITERATURE, ON ONE NUMBER, and it is flagged rather than resolved. The ductus venosus narration says it carries 'roughly half' of umbilical venous flow, and the model uses 0.50 so the picture agrees with the words a student is reading. Human fetal MRI in late gestation puts it nearer 0.30. Whoever reviews this should decide which one the corpus teaches; the build task is not the right place to overrule the narration silently.

THE INFERIOR VENA CAVA IS MODELLED AS ONE WELL-MIXED STREAM, and it should probably be two. Because the ductus venosus stream at 0.80 is a large part of it, holding the mixed inferior caval saturation at the narration's stated 0.70 forces the lower body's oxygen extraction down to about a tenth of the whole body's, which is not a fetus. In life the ductus venosus stream and the lower-body stream do not mix before the crista dividens - which is the same streaming the crista then exploits - so the 0.70 belongs to a stream, not to a mixture. This does not change any relation the scene asserts; it changes how the upper-to-lower extraction split is apportioned inside the solve.

THE CURRICULUM DOES NOT OFFER 3d_anatomy FOR THIS STRUCTURE. CURRICULUM.json lists preferred_modes ['sequence','diagram'] for 'Fetal circulation', so this scene's mode has been promoted past what the curriculum names. model3d-scene-spec-v2.md is explicit that this is the intended behaviour - 'a structure routed to diagram becomes a 3D scene the day a model for it exists, with no curriculum edit' - and deferred_modes keeps both the earlier options on the record. Noted because a reader comparing the two files will otherwise think one of them is wrong.

AXES. This model is +x = fetus's LEFT, +y = CRANIAL, +z = VENTRAL, which is NOT the LPS convention the spec's CROSS_SECTION table assumes for scanned meshes. Beat 3's cut is therefore normal to y, which in this model's frame is the transverse plane the narration asks for. The narration names no plane word, so nothing in it disagrees with the axis.

THE PLACENTA AND THE CORD ARE STILL DRAWN AFTER BIRTH. Geometry is built at every t and the views hide what is gone, so beat 7 and beat 8 do not show them. The umbilical vessels and the two ducts DO shrink with t, to three tenths of their fetal calibre, which is the ligamentum teres, venosum and arteriosum and the medial umbilical ligaments - the most examined line in the topic, made geometry rather than caption.

DUCT-DEPENDENT LESIONS ARE DESCRIBED, NOT SHOWN. Transposition, pulmonary atresia, critical coarctation and hypoplastic left heart each need a different heart, and this model builds one. Their narration is carried on beat 8, where the duct that keeps those babies alive is the thing on screen.

deferred_beats.title: How to answer any fetal circulation question
deferred_beats.narration: Four moves, in order. One: trace a red cell from placenta to placenta and name every vessel and shunt out loud — most marks are here. Two: at each shunt say what is being bypassed and which pressure difference drives the flow. Three: at birth, apply the two changes, lungs open and cord clamped, and let every closure follow from them. Four: name the remnant. Answer in that order and you never have to memorise the diagram as a picture.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: It is exam technique, not anatomy. There is no frame it could change: it describes the ORDER to say things in, and every structure it names is already shown by the view that teaches it. Rendered as a view it would be beat 2's frame with different words over it, which is what RENDER-STANDARD means by a beat that is text.
deferred_beats.belongs_in: the topic's revision notes, or as the scene's closing text panel — it is the best summary in this scene and it should not be a 3D beat
